answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks for independent counterparties, with each payout locked until the buyer confirms delivery and a random sample passes audit. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across a plume of accounts does not multiply trusted weight; each must build separate, costly records. The attacker pays deposits, labor, and audit risk per account, while a knoll of colluding identities still cannot validate one another. Even an ember of genuine work takes time to accumulate.
